texts: good. the Council, the emergency meeting and the whole day-17 afternoon time are covered, and the Council is correctly treated as one body rather than distributed over members. Note only that the times sit on the holding rather than on the meeting itself, so "when was the meeting?" has to be asked through the holding event — nothing to reword.

mixed: every atom emitted is true, but "that afternoon" is attached to the deciding rather than to the beginning of the additions, so the parse records when the Council decided and leaves the additions' start time unstated. If you mean the additions were to start that afternoon, put the time in a finite clause where it cannot detach: "The Council decided that the salt-bloom additions would begin that afternoon."

good. Hesper, the distributing, the pouches and the Cliff Path keepers as recipients all land. "Pouches of salt-bloom" is carried as one fused kind rather than as a containment relation, and "the keepers of the Cliff Path" as a loose possession link — both are holes in the instruction set rather than lost content, so leave the sentence as it stands.
good. the speaking, the Council as speaker and the Northcove keepers as addressees are all covered, with the addressees in the recipient role rather than a spatial one.
good. the whole need-state is denied as a single bundle with its past tense inside, which is the right shape for a plain negation.

mixed: the recording, the cold snap and the ledger all land, but "in the ledger" is filed as a spatial location of the recording event — where the recording took place — instead of the medium the record went into, which is what the sentence means. To steer clear of that reading, write it as a transfer into the ledger: "The Council added the cold snap to the ledger."
